The first risk is that supply chain constraints govern the pace at which demand converts into revenue for the next several quarters [D3]. That risk would be confirmed by fourth quarter revenue landing below the low end of the guidance range of $1.930 billion while orders hold at or above $2 billion [D1].

The second risk is that profitability faces a higher comparison bar because the one-time tariff impacts in fiscal 2026 will not repeat [D3]. That risk would be confirmed by operating margin in a subsequent quarter falling below the long-term target range of 31% to 32% [D3].

The third risk is that growth is concentrated in AI infrastructure spending, where hyperscalers are roughly 10% of the business directly and wireline orders more than doubled [D3]. That risk would be confirmed by fourth quarter orders coming in below the $2.091 billion booked in the third quarter rather than the slight increase management expects [D1].

The fourth risk is that integration of recent acquisitions and the related cost synergies fall short of the 80% to 90% of the $100 million target management expects on a run rate basis exiting the fiscal year [D3]. That risk would be confirmed by management reporting synergy realization below that range at the fiscal year end [D3].

The fifth risk is that non-GAAP results overstate core performance, given non-GAAP net income of $531 million against GAAP net income of $397 million in the latest quarter [D1]. That risk would be confirmed by non-GAAP net income rising in a quarter when GAAP net income falls [D1].
